newsitem.title: USA: USAir won't be part of AMR, British Airways pact.
newsitem.headline: USAir won't be part of AMR, British Airways pact.

text.p: USAir Group Inc. Chairman Stephen Wolf said there was no room for USAir in the proposed international marketing agreement between AMR Corp's American Airlines and British Airways PLC, the Washington Post reported on Tuesday.
"We simply do not believe we can be a part of it," Wolf told the paper.
His comments signal a further rupture in USAir's relationship with British Air, which owns 24.6 percent of the U.S. airline.
American Airlines and British Air proposed a broad marketing agreement in June that, if approved, would allow the two carriers to dominate transatlantic flights between London and the United States.
Both welcomed USAir's continued involvement in the new alliance, but Wolf said, "We don't have a great deal of insight into what they're trying to do."

The newspaper quoted Wolf as saying that communication between USAir and British Air had basically ceased since USAir filed suit in July, seeking to break up its alliance with the foreign carrier and terming its deal with American Air a betrayal.
Wolf said he did not believe the U.S. government would give USAir the necessary antitrust immunity to participate in the American Air-British Airways deal.
